validation_gates.reason: These paths are under _model.CONTROL_PREFIXES and the tracked state keeps permissions.modify_control_logic false. The repository owner explicitly authorized this control-logic change in the authoring session before any edit. The tracked state and its permissions are unchanged.

On main, repository_control._model.load_json, which the module docstring describes as strict JSON, accepted duplicate keys (last value wins, so a reader and the digest could disagree) and NaN/Infinity, and raised an uncaught UnicodeDecodeError for invalid UTF-8 and RecursionError for deep nesting instead of STATE_INPUT_INVALID or CONTEXT_INPUT_INVALID. It now rejects duplicates and non-standard constants the way the sibling helpers validate_control_source_availability.py and fetch_bounded_issue_comments.py already do, and reports every parse failure as an InputError. The new tests fail on the original code (8 tests and subtests).

The tracked state digest is unchanged (ab25ada4f8d2c5ee6d3d86bb798b2cb75f59f61f9da126be7f799d6011cc6b0c), validate-state still passes, every context fixture evaluates to the same outcome, and the 95 existing repository-control tests pass (101 with the new ones).

tests/validators/test_repository_control_cli.py adds 6 tests covering the digest, validate-state and evaluate commands, the outcome file against ci_outcome.schema.json, the exit-code vocabulary and nine unusable inputs. Branch coverage of validate_repository_control.py rises from 23% to 95% and of _model.py from 70% to 78%.
Each of four changes failed the suite: removing the duplicate-key hook, the constant hook, the RecursionError normalization or the root-object check.
ruff reports the same 4 pre-existing findings in the source files and none in the new test file. make repository-guardrails PASS.
